title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Discover the unique rituals and storied customs of the College of Charleston, from white-clad graduations in the Cistern Yard to the superstitions of Porter's Lodge.

cards.title: White Dresses and Dinner Jackets
cards.subtitle: A formal alternative to caps and gowns
cards.notes: Skip the polyester robes; spring graduates wear white dresses or white dinner jackets with a red rose or boutonniere, a tradition dating back to the early 20th century.
cards.short_summary: CofC spring graduates wear formal white attire instead of traditional academic regalia.
cards.evidence_claim: At the College of Charleston, spring graduates completing their undergraduate degrees do not don robes or caps — instead, they wear white dresses or white dinner jackets.
cards.access_notes: Visible during the annual spring commencement ceremony in May.

cards.title: The 'Know Thyself' Passage
cards.subtitle: Entering and exiting the Cistern Yard
cards.notes: Walk through the archway on your first day for Convocation and exit through it after Graduation to symbolize your journey into the world.
cards.short_summary: Students pass through the Porter's Lodge archway at the start and end of their college careers.
cards.evidence_claim: Students at the College of Charleston pass through the arch at Porter's Lodge on their first day... Upon graduation in the spring, students exit the Cistern Yard by passing underneath the same arch.
cards.access_notes: The archway is located on George Street and is accessible to the public.

cards.title: Don't Cross the Cistern
cards.subtitle: A jinx on your graduation date
cards.notes: Avoid walking across the raised grassy oval of the Cistern before you graduate, or legend says you won't finish your degree on time.
cards.short_summary: A campus superstition warns students not to walk across the Cistern until they graduate.
cards.evidence_claim: In the 21st century, however, some students believe that walking across the Cistern before finishing their education will jinx their chances of graduating.
cards.source_title: Get Ready For Graduation: Four Facts About the Cistern
cards.access_notes: The Cistern Yard is a central campus green open to students and visitors.

cards.title: Turning the Ring
cards.subtitle: A signet-style rite of passage
cards.notes: Wear your school ring with the seal upside down until commencement, then turn it right-side up to signify your status as an alumnus.
cards.short_summary: Graduates turn their school rings right-side up during the commencement ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: At Commencement, College of Charleston students are called upon to 'turn the ring'... so the seal is facing right side up as they go out into the world.
cards.access_notes: The ring ceremony and turning of the ring occur annually for eligible students.

cards.title: Pep Supper
cards.subtitle: A century of spirit and service
cards.notes: Attend this high-energy dance competition and food drive that kicks off basketball season, a tradition that has evolved over nearly 100 years.
cards.short_summary: Pep Supper is a long-standing tradition featuring a dance contest and food drive for the Lowcountry Food Bank.
cards.evidence_claim: Pep Supper is one of the oldest traditions at the College, dating back almost 100 years... transformed the celebration into a weeklong fundraiser and food drive.
cards.source_title: CofC Alumni Pep Supper Supports Fraternity, Sorority Life
cards.access_notes: Held annually in the fall, typically at the TD Arena.

cards.title: Signing the Book
cards.subtitle: Official entry into the academic community
cards.notes: Join your classmates during Convocation to officially sign the College's ledger, marking your formal induction into the student body.
cards.short_summary: New students sign a formal ledger during Convocation to mark their entry into the College.
cards.evidence_claim: Students at the College of Charleston pass through the arch at Porter's Lodge on their first day and enter the Cistern Yard to officially sign 'the book.'
cards.access_notes: Occurs during the annual Convocation ceremony in August.

cards.title: The Ghosts of Berry Hall
cards.subtitle: Campus legends of the old orphanage
cards.notes: Listen for the sounds of phantom marbles or children's voices in this residence hall, built on the site of a former orphanage.
cards.short_summary: Berry Residence Hall is the subject of long-standing campus ghost stories related to its history as an orphanage site.
cards.evidence_claim: Students then reported hearing distant voices and laughter of children late into the night. Some students also said that they were awakened by the sound of marbles cascading across the floor.
cards.source_title: 3 Tales of College of Charleston Ghosts
cards.access_notes: Residence hall access is restricted to students, but the exterior is visible on St. Philip Street.

cards.title: Maroon Mayhem
cards.subtitle: The ultimate back-to-school bash
cards.notes: Celebrate the start of the year with this street festival featuring games, food, and music right in the heart of campus.
cards.short_summary: Maroon Mayhem is an annual street festival held during the first week of classes.
cards.evidence_claim: A good time was had by all at the 2023 Maroon Mayhem, the College's annual street festival celebrating the return of students to campus.
cards.source_title: College of Charleston Photos of the Week
cards.access_notes: Held annually in August during the 'Weeks of Welcome.'

cards.entity_name: Ring Night at the President's House
cards.title: Instilling History in the Rings
cards.subtitle: A night at 6 Glebe Street
cards.notes: Before the ring ceremony, all student rings spend the night in the President's House to be 'instilled' with the College's 250-year history.
cards.short_summary: Student rings are housed in the historic President's House the night before they are presented.
cards.evidence_claim: Tradition dictates that the night before each Ring Ceremony, the rings spend the night in the College's original classroom in the President's House at 6 Glebe Street.
cards.access_notes: The President's House is a private residence, but the tradition is part of the official ring program.

cards.title: Rubbing the Cougar Paw
cards.subtitle: Luck from the campus mascot
cards.notes: Visit the Clyde the Cougar statues on campus for a photo op or a quick rub of the paw for good luck before a big game or exam.
cards.short_summary: Two statues of the mascot Clyde the Cougar serve as campus landmarks and symbols of school spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: Clyde the Cougar is beloved by young and old and is represented in two statues on campus.
cards.source_title: Traditions from the CofC Traditions App
cards.access_notes: Statues are located in Cougar Mall and near the TD Arena.
